capabilities: Tag notes by linking tag notes from a keywords list property
Build a tag hierarchy with broader links, multiple parents and cycle detection
Browse a sidebar tag tree with direct and descendant counts, filtering and rename
Convert existing #tags into tag notes with a previewed, git-committable bulk migration
List notes tagged with a tag or its subtree via query blocks and exported Bases filters
disambiguation: Not a tag-description or tag-page plugin; the tag note itself replaces the #tag as the source of truth.
extras: Documentation ships as an interactive demo vault (also readable on GitHub); publishes a read-only API (api.d.ts) for other plugins; manifest notes it has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff.
motivation: The author frames bare tags as limited: "A #tag is a bare string. It cannot carry a description, aliases or properties of its own".
problem: Bare #tags cannot carry descriptions, aliases or properties, are easy to misspell, and renaming means vault-wide search-and-replace, while tagging with links loses the tag hierarchy, Tags pane and typeahead suggestions.

relations.evidence: Overlaps on hierarchy: not about tags, so no tag counts
Same goal of a tag hierarchy: the hierarchy lives in the tag notes' own broader links
Inverse direction: its tag page describes a #tag that stays the source of truth
Same goal of joining notes and tags: keeps the #tag as the source
Same goal of listing notes by tag: the tag is a note rather than a #tag

summary: Makes each tag a note: tagging is linking tag notes, with a hierarchy, a tag tree with counts, subtree queries and conversion of existing #tags.
